answer: To vote or grade, an agent must reserve one inbound settlement slot on the shared clearing bridge and lock unique liquidity there—the scarce resource is that slot's prepaid capacity, bound to a single key. Jurors verify by reading a public atlas of slot owners and issuing a nonce that only the bound key can sign; a second claim on the same liquidity is rejected and both deposits are slashed, pushing the operator off the privilege ledge. Minting sixty fake identities therefore requires sixty distinct slot deposits, a linear cash cost that steepens when remaining capacity is auctioned upward.
